q_and_p_series.purpose: 2(a) same-condition repetition distribution on the PREVIOUS generation + 2(b) the two ORD-0257 cells re-run on the now-PUBLISHED generation
q_and_p_series.generation_note: Publish line moved at 15:53 by the commander: PUBLISHED = index-DJEINrOl.js + index-COUUKhbU.css built from 027d65ed381fbb4bfb81a07a7ae20a9f293454e1 (his swap receipt evidence/deploy/swap_027d65e_0923_1553.json, blob 89e91c7e369fc8f3: new_index_refs = those two, assets_union.already_identical lists both, arm J_name_content_binding = GREEN, overall GREEN). The generation I called 'new' in ORD-0257 is therefore now the published one, and CrAwWm5f is the PREVIOUS generation (backup anchor dist_bak_154923_1790149763821685500).

published.identity_argument: same content-hashed basenames the commander's swap receipt names as deployed + same byte lengths; Vite basenames are content hashes, so name equality is the byte-identity claim, and arm J on his side checked name/content binding
published.my_build_provenance: vite build of my own `git archive 027d65ed381fbb4bfb81a07a7ae20a9f293454e1` export (ORD-0257)

previous.sha256_index-CrAwWm5f.js: 9fd89456daf12bcab4bb775c8a8522d50628a... see receipt (matches the sha256 in the commander's swap receipt for generation_OLD exactly)
previous.identity_argument: his swap receipt records generation_OLD probe sha256 9fd89456daf12bca... and disk_bytes 1234802; my served file is 1234802 B with the same sha256 => byte-identical to the generation the user was on until 15:53

q_and_p_series.instrument: 390x844, hasTouch, isMobile, deviceScaleFactor 3, locale zh-CN; double press = two element.click() inside ONE task (t0/t1 identical ms) because two real touch taps cannot be same-tick; sheet opened by a real tap on [data-testid=hub-plan-with-ai]; request text 31 chars typed via the textarea

Q_series_previous_generation.condition: one journey (ae79fbf1), same-tick double press, repeated; gate between rounds = the sheet's own busy flag (button label 开始规划 and not disabled) + 4-6 s margin

rounds.note: statuses from the DB/endpoint-histogram delta, page had navigated away before my read

distribution.which_leg_loses: 4/4 of the losses were the LATER leg of the pair (same as R7's 3/3)

Q_series_previous_generation.reconciliation: backend access log 200 34 -> 45 and 500 10 -> 14 across Q+P = +11 x 200 +4 x 500 = 15 posts, and hard-fail tracebacks 16 -> 20 = +4, i.e. exactly one unhandled OperationalError per 500
Q_series_previous_generation.extra_reading: the sheet's busy flag is NOT ref-counted: with both legs of a pair in flight, the leg that returns first flips the button back to 开始规划 while the other is still running (observed at the Q2 fire: Q1 leg1 resolved at 08:55:59, i.e. after Q2 was fired at 08:55:33)

P_series_published_generation.condition: same as Q series (one journey ae79fbf1, same-tick double press, 3 rounds) + the earlier arm on journey cc5e67c4 (P0)

cell_summary_hitbox.comparison: previous generation measured 311 x 14 in ORD-0257; published generation measures 311.3 x 44 => ORD-0247 is now 现网验过, not just 树里验过

caveats: Q-series rounds were spaced by the sheet's busy flag, which the extra_reading above shows is not reliable while both legs are in flight; so Q2..Q6 are NOT lab-isolated - another POST may have been in flight. I report the condition as measured rather than claiming isolation; Q1 is the one round that was demonstrably isolated (78 s after the previous activity ended).
Q6's statuses come from the endpoint-histogram + DB rows, not from the page (the page had moved on); labelled as such.
The lane still has several hub pages polling /twin, so background write pressure is higher than a real single phone; the 25.6%/4-in-12 rates are lane rates, not user rates.
Runs mostly end FAILED_EXTERNAL (the pending-revocation DeepSeek key), which lengthens write windows; shape with a healthy AI is untested.
No product code changed, no demo/reset, no writes to _live.db/_preview.db/:4781/:4782/:8693 or the tunnel.
